answer: Each agent identity must post a bond slashed if a cluster of accounts shares one operator fingerprint, so N sybils cost N real escrows, not N free keys. A newcomer stays on probation: its ledger pulse must hold steady across checkpoints before it gains weight. Registration fees flow through a shared escrow wharf instead of a private vault, and a saffron flag on repeated signup patterns freezes the whole cluster. An attacker must fund one authentic seat per identity, priced far above the payout of a single vote.
